21	  subtype A u ->

37	(* A typing of a stem at a function type is principal at the
38	   corresponding stem type. *)
39	Lemma stem_fun_principal: forall M gamma u ty,
40	  program M ->
41	  (forall gamma ty, derive gamma M ty -> subtype (program_type M) ty) ->
42	  derive gamma (Node @ M) (Funty u ty) ->
43	  subtype (Stem (program_type M)) (Funty u ty).
44	Proof.
45	  intros M gamma u ty Hp IH Hd.
46	  inversion Hd; subst.
47	  inversion H3; subst.
48	  pose proof (IH _ _ H5) as HA.
49	  eauto 15 with triage.

58	  - simpl. eauto 12 with triage.

35	Definition test : forall n m : nat, {n <= m} + {n > m} := ltac:(simple induction n; simple induction m; simpl in |- *; auto with arith;
36	intros m' H'; elim (H m'); auto with arith).

38	Definition le_lt : forall n m : nat, n <= m -> {n < m} + {n = m} := ltac:(simple induction n; simple induction m; simpl in |- *; auto with arith;
39	    intros m' H1 H2; elim (H m'); auto with arith).

41	Definition compare : forall n m : nat, {n < m} + {n = m} + {n > m} := ltac:(intros n m; elim (test n m); auto with arith;
42	    left; apply le_lt; trivial with arith).
43	
44	Definition relocate (i k n : nat) :=
45	  match test k i with
46	     | left _ => n+i
47	     | _ => i
48	  end.

52	Fixpoint lift_rec (L : dtype) : nat -> nat -> dtype :=
53	  fun k n =>
54	  match L with
55	  | Var i => Var (relocate i k n)
56	  | Leaf => Leaf
57	  | Stem ty => Stem (lift_rec ty k n)
58	  | Fork ty1 ty2 => Fork (lift_rec ty1 k n) (lift_rec ty2 k n)
59	  | Funty ty1 ty2 => Funty (lift_rec ty1 k n) (lift_rec ty2 k n)
60	  | Quant ty => Quant (lift_rec ty (S k) n)
61	  | Asf ty => Asf (lift_rec ty k n)
62	  end.
63	
64	Definition lift (n : nat) (ty : dtype) := lift_rec ty 0 n.
65	
66	Definition insert_Var (N : dtype) (i k : nat) :=
67	  match compare k i with
68	
69	     | inleft (left _) => Var (Nat.pred i)
70	     | inleft _ => lift k N
71	     | _ => Var i
72	  end.
73	
74	Fixpoint subst_rec (L : dtype) : dtype -> nat -> dtype :=
75	  fun (N : dtype) (k : nat) =>
76	  match L with
77	  | Var i => insert_Var N i k
78	  | Leaf => Leaf
79	  | Stem M => Stem (subst_rec M N k)
80	  | Fork M M' => Fork (subst_rec M N k) (subst_rec M' N k)
81	  | Funty M M' => Funty (subst_rec M N k) (subst_rec M' N k)
82	  | Quant M => Quant (subst_rec M N (S k))
83	  | Asf M => Asf (subst_rec M N k)
84	  end.

92	  end.

97	
98	Definition subst_rec_context uty k := map (fun (p:string * dtype)  => (fst p, subst_rec (snd p) uty k)).

100	Fixpoint normal_type gamma t :=

102	  | Ref x => get x gamma
103	  | Node => Some Leaf
104	  | Node @ t1 => match normal_type gamma t1 with | Some ty => Some (Stem ty) | _ => None end

109	    end
110	  | _ => None
111	  end.

113	Fixpoint quant n ty :=

115	  | 0 => ty
116	  | S n1 => quant n1 (Quant ty)
117	  end.
118	
119	Fixpoint quantf n ty :=
120	  match n with
121	  | 0 => ty
122	  | S n1 => quantf n1 (Asf ty)
123	  end.
124	
125	Fixpoint quanta bs ty :=
126	  match bs with
127	    nil => ty
128	  | true :: bs1 => quanta bs1 (Quant ty)
129	  | false :: bs1 => quanta bs1 (Asf ty)
130	  end.
131	
132	Fixpoint quant_count bs :=
133	  match bs with
134	    nil => 0
135	  | true :: bs1 => S (quant_count bs1)
136	  | false :: bs1 => quant_count bs1
137	  end.
138	
139	Fixpoint quant_to_quanta n :=
140	  match n with
141	  | 0 => nil
142	  | S n1 => true :: (quant_to_quanta n1)
143	  end.
144	
145	Fixpoint variant pos k ty :=
146	
147	
148	  match ty with
149	  | Var n => if k=?n then pos else true
150	  | Quant ty1 => variant pos (S k) ty1
151	  | Funty ty1 ty2 => variant (negb pos) k ty1 && variant pos k ty2
152	  | Leaf => true
153	  | Stem ty1 => variant pos k ty1
154	  | Fork ty1 ty2 => variant pos k ty1 && variant pos k ty2
155	  | Asf ty1 => variant pos k ty1
156	   end.

Require Import String Arith Lia Bool List Nat.

Require Import terms types subtypes derive.

Open Scope string_scope.

Open Scope nat_scope.

Set Default Proof Using "Type".

(* A small hint database for the subtyping and typing rules. *)
Create HintDb triage.

Hint Constructors subtype : triage.
Hint Constructors derive : triage.
Hint Constructors program : triage.

(* Applications of a leaf and of a stem. *)
Lemma subtype_leaf_app: forall A u ty,
  subtype Leaf (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype A u ->
  subtype (Stem A) ty.
Proof.
  intros. eauto 15 with triage.
Qed.

Lemma subtype_stem_app: forall A B u ty,
  subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype B u ->
  subtype (Fork A B) ty.
Proof.
  intros. eauto 15 with triage.
Qed.

Hint Resolve subtype_leaf_app subtype_stem_app : triage.

(* A typing of a stem at a function type is principal at the
   corresponding stem type. *)
Lemma stem_fun_principal: forall M gamma u ty,
  program M ->
  (forall gamma ty, derive gamma M ty -> subtype (program_type M) ty) ->
  derive gamma (Node @ M) (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype (Stem (program_type M)) (Funty u ty).
Proof.
  intros M gamma u ty Hp IH Hd.
  inversion Hd; subst.
  inversion H3; subst.
  pose proof (IH _ _ H5) as HA.
  eauto 15 with triage.
Qed.

Hint Resolve stem_fun_principal : triage.

Theorem programs_have_types: forall p gamma, program p -> derive gamma p (program_type p).
Proof.
  intros p gamma Hp. induction Hp.
  - simpl. eauto 10 with triage.
  - simpl. eauto 12 with triage.
  - simpl. eauto 20 with triage.
Qed.

Theorem programs_have_principal_types:
  forall p, program p ->
            forall gamma ty, derive gamma p ty -> subtype (program_type p) ty.
Proof.
  intros p Hp. induction Hp; intros gamma ty Hd.
  - simpl. inversion Hd; subst. eauto with triage.
  - simpl. inversion Hd; subst. inversion H3; subst.
    pose proof (IHHp _ _ H5) as HA.
    eauto 15 with triage.
  - simpl. inversion Hd; subst.
    pose proof (IHHp1 _ _ H5) as HM.
    pose proof (IHHp2 _ _ H4) as HN.
    eauto 20 with triage.
Qed.

Definition test : forall n m : nat, {n <= m} + {n > m} := ltac:(simple induction n; simple induction m; simpl in |- *; auto with arith;
intros m' H'; elim (H m'); auto with arith).

Definition le_lt : forall n m : nat, n <= m -> {n < m} + {n = m} := ltac:(simple induction n; simple induction m; simpl in |- *; auto with arith;
    intros m' H1 H2; elim (H m'); auto with arith).

Definition compare : forall n m : nat, {n < m} + {n = m} + {n > m} := ltac:(intros n m; elim (test n m); auto with arith;
    left; apply le_lt; trivial with arith).

Definition relocate (i k n : nat) :=
  match test k i with
     | left _ => n+i
     | _ => i
  end.

Definition relocatek1 k i := relocate i k 1.

Fixpoint lift_rec (L : dtype) : nat -> nat -> dtype :=
  fun k n =>
  match L with
  | Var i => Var (relocate i k n)
  | Leaf => Leaf
  | Stem ty => Stem (lift_rec ty k n)
  | Fork ty1 ty2 => Fork (lift_rec ty1 k n) (lift_rec ty2 k n)
  | Funty ty1 ty2 => Funty (lift_rec ty1 k n) (lift_rec ty2 k n)
  | Quant ty => Quant (lift_rec ty (S k) n)
  | Asf ty => Asf (lift_rec ty k n)
  end.

Definition lift (n : nat) (ty : dtype) := lift_rec ty 0 n.

Definition insert_Var (N : dtype) (i k : nat) :=
  match compare k i with

     | inleft (left _) => Var (Nat.pred i)
     | inleft _ => lift k N
     | _ => Var i
  end.

Fixpoint subst_rec (L : dtype) : dtype -> nat -> dtype :=
  fun (N : dtype) (k : nat) =>
  match L with
  | Var i => insert_Var N i k
  | Leaf => Leaf
  | Stem M => Stem (subst_rec M N k)
  | Fork M M' => Fork (subst_rec M N k) (subst_rec M' N k)
  | Funty M M' => Funty (subst_rec M N k) (subst_rec M' N k)
  | Quant M => Quant (subst_rec M N (S k))
  | Asf M => Asf (subst_rec M N k)
  end.

Definition subst (M N : dtype) := subst_rec M N 0.

Fixpoint get x (gamma: list (string * dtype)) :=
  match gamma with
  | (s,ty)::gamma1 => if (s =? x)%string then Some ty else get x gamma1

Require Import String Arith Lia Bool List Nat.

Require Import terms types.

Open Scope string_scope.

Open Scope nat_scope.

Set Default Proof Using "Type".

Definition omega21_ty := program_type omega21.

Definition omega22_ty := program_type omega22.

Definition omega2_ty := (Fork (Stem omega21_ty) omega22_ty).

Definition eval_ty := quant 1 (Funty (Var 0) (Asf (Var 0))).

Definition eager_ty := quant 2 (Funty (Funty (Var 0) (Var 1)) (Funty (Var 0) (Var 1))).

Definition bfff_aug uty := Fork (Stem (Fork Leaf eval_ty)) (Asf uty).

Definition bffs_aug uty := Fork (Stem (Fork Leaf eager_ty)) (bfff_aug uty).

Inductive subtype : dtype -> dtype -> Prop :=

| sub_zero : forall ty, subtype ty ty
| sub_trans : forall ty1 ty2 ty3, subtype ty1 ty2 -> subtype ty2 ty3 -> subtype ty1 ty3

| sub_stem : forall uty1 uty2, subtype uty1 uty2 -> subtype (Stem uty1) (Stem uty2)
| sub_fork : forall uty1 uty2 vty1 vty2, subtype uty1 uty2 -> subtype vty1 vty2 ->
                                         subtype (Fork uty1 vty1) (Fork uty2 vty2)
| sub_asf : forall uty1 uty2, subtype uty1 uty2 -> subtype (Asf uty1) (Asf uty2)
| sub_funty : forall uty1 uty2 vty1 vty2, subtype uty2 uty1 -> subtype vty1 vty2 ->
                                          subtype (Funty uty1 vty1) (Funty uty2 vty2)
| sub_quant : forall vty1 vty2,  subtype vty1 vty2 -> subtype (Quant vty1) (Quant vty2)

| sub_quant_stem: forall uty, subtype (Quant (Stem uty)) (Stem (Quant uty))
| sub_quant_fork: forall uty vty, subtype (Quant (Fork uty vty)) (Fork (Quant uty) (Quant vty))
| sub_quant_asf: forall uty, subtype (Quant (Asf uty)) (Asf (Quant uty))
| sub_dist: forall uty vty, subtype (Quant (Funty uty vty)) (Funty (Quant uty) (Quant vty))

| sub_inst : forall ty u,  subtype (Quant ty) (subst ty u)
| sub_lift: forall ty, subtype ty (Quant (lift 1 ty))

| sub_leaf_fun:forall uty,  subtype Leaf (Funty uty (Stem uty))
| sub_stem_fun: forall uty vty, subtype (Stem uty) (Funty vty (Fork uty vty))

| sub_fork_leaf: forall uty vty, subtype (Fork Leaf uty) (Funty vty uty)
| sub_fork_stem: forall uty vty wty,
    subtype (Fork (Stem (Funty uty (Funty vty wty))) (Funty uty vty)) (Funty uty wty)
| sub_fork_fork_leaf: forall uty vty wty,
    subtype (Fork (Fork uty vty) wty) (Funty Leaf uty)
| sub_fork_fork_stem:
    forall uty vty1 vty2 wty,
      subtype (Fork (Fork uty (Funty vty1 vty2)) wty) (Funty (Stem vty1) vty2)
| sub_fork_fork_fork:
    forall uty vty wty1 wty2 wty3,
      subtype (Fork (Fork uty vty) (Funty wty1 (Funty wty2 wty3))) (Funty (Fork wty1 wty2) wty3)

| sub_recursion:
    forall k uty vty,
      subtype omega2_ty
              (Funty
                 omega2_ty
                 (Funty
                    (Funty (quant k (Funty uty vty)) (quant k (Funty uty vty)))
                    (quant k (Funty uty vty))))
| sub_tree: forall ty uty,
    covariant ty ->
    subtype (Fork
               (Fork
                  (subst ty Leaf)
                  (quant 1 (Funty (Var 0) (subst (lift_rec ty 1 1) (Stem (Var 0))))))
               (quant
                  2
                  (Funty
                     (Var 1)
                     (Funty (Var 0) (subst (lift_rec ty 1 2) (Fork (Var 1) (Var 0)))))
            ))
            (Funty uty (subst ty uty))
| sub_to_asf: forall ty, subtype ty (Asf ty)
| sub_from_asf: forall uty vty, subtype (Asf (Funty uty vty)) (Funty uty vty)
| sub_bffs: forall uty vty, subtype (Fork (Stem (bffs_aug uty)) (Asf vty)) (Asf (Fork (Stem uty) vty))
| sub_bfff : forall uty vty wty, subtype (Fork (Fork uty (Asf vty)) (bfff_aug wty))
                                         (Asf (Fork (Fork uty vty) wty))
.

# 208 — Typed tree calculus: principal types

## Task

Show that the canonical type of a tree-calculus program is derivable and is a subtype of every type assignable to it.

Prove all of the following declarations in `Task.v`:

- `programs_have_types`
- `programs_have_principal_types`

## Input

- `input/Task.v` is the target file; in the proof workspace, it is `Task.v`.
- Any other supplied `.v` files provide support definitions. Use `_CoqProject` for the source list and library mappings.
- Rocq version: 9.1.0. Local prerequisites: none beyond the Rocq standard library.

The project already includes the listed dependencies; do not install anything for the proof run.

## Rules

- Edit only `Task.v` in the submitted solution. You may add helper definitions and lemmas there. Keep all supplied definitions and target names, statements, and hypotheses unchanged. Do not change support files or `_CoqProject`.
- Do not use `Admitted`, `admit`, or `Abort` in the submitted solution. Do not add axioms or new global assumptions (including via `Axiom`, `Parameter`, or `Conjecture`), disable kernel checks (such as guard, positivity, or universe checking), or use equivalent shortcuts.
- Work offline. Use only the supplied input and permitted local libraries. Do not look up, copy, or import an existing proof of any target.

## Deliverable

A completed `Task.v` that compiles with Rocq using the supplied project configuration, with every listed target proved and no open goals.

To verify, run `make` from the project root. All project dependencies are included.

Require Import String Arith Lia Bool List Nat.

Require Import terms types subtypes derive.

Open Scope string_scope.

Open Scope nat_scope.

Set Default Proof Using "Type".

Theorem programs_have_types: forall p gamma, program p -> derive gamma p (program_type p).

Theorem programs_have_principal_types:
  forall p, program p ->
            forall gamma ty, derive gamma p ty -> subtype (program_type p) ty.

Require Import String Arith Lia Bool List Nat.
Require Import Triage.terms Triage.types Triage.subtypes Triage.derive.
Open Scope string_scope. Open Scope nat_scope. Open Scope tree_scope.
Set Default Proof Using "Type".

Fixpoint qcount (X : dtype) : nat :=
  match X with Quant X0 => S (qcount X0) | _ => 0 end.
Fixpoint qbody (X : dtype) : dtype :=
  match X with Quant X0 => qbody X0 | _ => X end.
Fixpoint beh_body (n : nat) (X : dtype) (d : dtype) {struct X} : dtype :=
  match X with
  | Leaf => Stem d | Stem A => Fork (quant n A) d | Funty a b => quant n b
  | Asf X0 => beh_body n X0 d | Quant X0 => beh_body (S n) X0 d
  | Fork _ _ => Leaf | Var _ => Leaf end.
Fixpoint beh (X : dtype) (d : dtype) {struct X} : dtype :=
  match X with
  | Leaf => Stem d | Stem A => Fork A d | Funty a b => b | Asf X0 => beh X0 d
  | Quant X0 => beh_body (S (qcount X0)) (qbody X0) d
  | Fork _ _ => Leaf | Var _ => Leaf end.
Definition behQ (X d : dtype) := beh (Quant X) d.

Fixpoint Good (X : dtype) : Prop :=
  match X with
  | Leaf => True | Stem _ => True | Funty _ _ => True | Fork _ _ => False
  | Asf X0 => Good X0 | Quant X0 => Good X0 | Var _ => False end.

Fixpoint InDom (d X : dtype) : Prop :=
  match X with
  | Funty a b => subtype d a
  | Asf X0 => InDom d X0
  | Quant X0 => InDomQ d X0
  | _ => True
  end
with InDomQ (d X : dtype) : Prop :=
  match X with
  | Funty a b => subtype d (Quant a)
  | Asf a => InDomQ d a
  | Quant a => subtype d (Quant (Quant a))
  | _ => True
  end.

Hint Constructors subtype : sb.

(* Auxiliary facts to be proved *)
Lemma behQ_mono : forall a b, subtype a b -> forall d,
  subtype (behQ a d) (behQ b d).
Admitted.
Lemma beh_inst : forall ty u d, subtype (behQ ty d) (beh (subst ty u) d).
Admitted.
Lemma beh_lift : forall ty d, subtype (beh ty d) (behQ (lift 1 ty) d).
Admitted.
Lemma behQ_lift_quant : forall ty d, subtype (behQ ty d) (beh (Quant (Quant (lift 1 (Quant ty)))) d).
Admitted.
(* maybe nested cases *)

Lemma beh_mono_good : forall X Y, subtype X Y -> Good X ->
  forall d, InDom d Y -> subtype (beh X d) (beh Y d).
Proof.
  intros X Y H. induction H; intros Hg d Hdom; simpl in *; try (eauto 8 with sb).
  - (* stem *) apply sub_fork; [assumption|apply sub_zero].
  - (* asf *) apply sub_asf. apply IHsubtype; [exact Hg|exact Hdom].
  - (* funty *) apply IHsubtype0. assumption.
  - (* quant *) apply behQ_mono. assumption.
  - (* quant_stem *) apply sub_zero.
  - (* quant_asf *) apply sub_zero.
  - (* dist *) apply sub_zero.
  - (* inst *) apply beh_inst.
  - (* lift *) apply beh_lift.
  - (* leaf_fun *) apply sub_stem. exact Hdom.
  - (* stem_fun *) apply sub_fork; [apply sub_zero| exact Hdom].
Abort.

| sub_leaf_fun:forall uty,  subtype Leaf (Funty uty (Stem uty))

| derive_node : forall gamma uty, subtype Leaf uty -> derive gamma Node uty

| Leaf : dtype
| Stem : dtype -> dtype
| Fork : dtype -> dtype -> dtype
| Asf : dtype -> dtype
.

Fixpoint  program_type p :=
  match p with
  | Node => Leaf
  | p1 @ p2 =>
    match program_type p1 with

Require Import Arith Lia Bool List Nat Datatypes String.

Set Default Proof Using "Type".

Open Scope string_scope.

Declare Scope tree_scope.

Global Open Scope tree_scope.

Inductive Tree:  Set :=
  | Ref : string -> Tree
  | Node : Tree
  | App : Tree -> Tree -> Tree
.

Notation "△" := Node : tree_scope.

Notation "x @ y" := (App x y) (at level 65, left associativity) : tree_scope.

Definition K := △ @ △.

Definition S1 x := △ @ (△@x).

Definition Sop := S1 (K @ Node) @ Node.

Definition I := S1 K @ K.

Definition KI := K@I.

Inductive program : Tree -> Prop :=
| pr_leaf : program △
| pr_stem : forall M, program M -> program (△ @ M)
| pr_fork : forall M N, program M -> program N -> program (△ @ M@ N)
.

Inductive t_red1 : Tree -> Tree -> Prop :=
| k_red : forall y z, t_red1 (△ @ △ @ y @ z) y
| s_red: forall (x y z : Tree), t_red1 (△ @ (△ @ x) @ y @ z) (x @ z @ (y @ z))
| leaf_red: forall (w x y : Tree), t_red1 (△ @ (△ @ w @ x) @ y @ Node) w
| stem_red: forall (w x y z : Tree), t_red1 (△ @ (△ @ w @ x) @ y @ (Node @ z)) (x @ z)
| fork_red: forall (w x y z1 z2 : Tree), t_red1 (△ @ (△ @ w @ x) @ y @ (Node @ z1 @ z2)) (y @ z1 @ z2)
| appl_red : forall M M' N, t_red1 M M' -> t_red1 (M@N) (M'@N)
| appr_red : forall M N N', t_red1 N N' -> t_red1 (M@N) (M@N')
.

Inductive multi_step : (Tree -> Tree -> Prop) -> Tree -> Tree -> Prop :=
  | zero_red : forall red M, multi_step red M M
  | succ_red : forall (red: Tree-> Tree -> Prop) M N P,
                   red M N -> multi_step red N P -> multi_step red M P
.

Definition t_red := multi_step t_red1.

Definition transitive red := forall (M N P: Tree), red M N -> red N P -> red M P.

Definition preserves_appl (red : Tree -> Tree -> Prop) :=
forall M N M', red M M' -> red (M@N) (M'@ N).

Definition preserves_appr (red : Tree -> Tree -> Prop) :=
forall M N N', red N N' -> red (M@N) (M@N').

Definition preserves_app (red : Tree -> Tree -> Prop) :=
forall M M', red M M' -> forall N N', red N N' -> red (M@N) (M'@N').

Fixpoint substitute M x N :=
  match M with
  | Ref y => if eqb x y then N else Ref y
  | △ => △
  | M1 @ M2 => (substitute M1 x N) @ (substitute M2 x N)
end.

Fixpoint bracket x M :=
match M with
| Ref y =>  if eqb x y then I else (K@ (Ref y))
| △ => K@ △
| App M1 M2 => S1 (bracket x M1) @ (bracket x M2)
end
.

Fixpoint occurs x M :=
  match M with
  | Ref y => eqb x y
  | △ => false
  | M1@ M2 => (occurs x M1) || (occurs x M2)
  end.

Fixpoint star x M :=
  match M with
  | Ref y =>  if eqb x y then I else (K@ (Ref y))
  | △ => K@ △
  | App M1 M2 => if occurs x (M1 @ M2)

  end.

| is_Node : combination △
| is_App : forall M N, combination M -> combination N -> combination (M@ N)
.

Inductive active: Tree -> Prop :=
| active_ref: forall x, active (Ref x)
| active_app: forall M N, active M -> active (M@N)
.

Inductive normal : Tree -> Prop :=

| nf_leaf : normal △

.

Require Import String Arith Lia Bool List Nat.

Require Import terms types subtypes derive.

Open Scope string_scope.

Open Scope nat_scope.

Set Default Proof Using "Type".

(* A small hint database for the subtyping and typing rules. *)
Create HintDb triage.

Hint Constructors subtype : triage.
Hint Constructors derive : triage.
Hint Constructors program : triage.

(* Applications of a leaf and of a stem. *)
Lemma subtype_leaf_app: forall A u ty,
  subtype Leaf (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype A u ->
  subtype (Stem A) ty.
Proof.
  intros. eauto 15 with triage.
Qed.

Lemma subtype_stem_app: forall A B u ty,
  subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype B u ->
  subtype (Fork A B) ty.
Proof.
  intros. eauto 15 with triage.
Qed.

Hint Resolve subtype_leaf_app subtype_stem_app : triage.

(* A typing of a stem at a function type is principal at the
   corresponding stem type. *)
Lemma stem_fun_principal: forall M gamma u ty,
  program M ->
  (forall gamma ty, derive gamma M ty -> subtype (program_type M) ty) ->
  derive gamma (Node @ M) (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype (Stem (program_type M)) (Funty u ty).
Proof.
  intros M gamma u ty Hp IH Hd.
  inversion Hd; subst.
  inversion H3; subst.
  pose proof (IH _ _ H5) as HA.
  eauto 15 with triage.
Qed.

Hint Resolve stem_fun_principal : triage.

Theorem programs_have_types: forall p gamma, program p -> derive gamma p (program_type p).
Proof.
  intros p gamma Hp. induction Hp.
  - simpl. eauto 10 with triage.
  - simpl. eauto 12 with triage.
  - simpl. eauto 20 with triage.
Qed.

Theorem programs_have_principal_types:
  forall p, program p ->
            forall gamma ty, derive gamma p ty -> subtype (program_type p) ty.
Proof.
  intros p Hp. induction Hp; intros gamma ty Hd.
  - simpl. inversion Hd; subst. eauto with triage.
  - simpl. inversion Hd; subst. inversion H3; subst.
    pose proof (IHHp _ _ H5) as HA.
    eauto 15 with triage.
  - simpl. inversion Hd; subst.
    pose proof (IHHp1 _ _ H5) as HM.
    pose proof (IHHp2 _ _ H4) as HN.
    eauto 20 with triage.
Qed.

    + exfalso. lia.

Lemma subst_lift_rec : forall X k u, subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) u k = X.
Proof.
  induction X; intros k u; simpl; auto.
  - apply insert_relocate_k.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.

Lemma subst_lift1 : forall X u, subst (lift 1 X) u = X.
Proof.

  eapply sub_trans.
  - apply sub_lift.
  - change (subtype (Quant (Stem (Quant (lift_rec u 1 1)))) (Quant (Stem u))).
    apply sub_quant, sub_stem.
    eapply sub_trans.
    + apply sub_inst.
    + rewrite subst_lift_rec11. apply sub_zero.

Proof.
  intros A a.
  eapply sub_trans.
  - apply sub_lift.

                    (Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a))).

    + apply sub_zero.
    + eapply sub_trans.

Require Import String Arith Lia Bool List Nat.

Require Import terms types subtypes derive.

Open Scope string_scope.
Open Scope nat_scope.

Set Default Proof Using "Type".

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Scratch / partial solution.

   This file is a *partial* attempt.  It compiles with Admitted placeholders
   (Admitted is allowed in scratch files only; the submitted Task.v must not
   contain it).  The fully proved parts are marked accordingly.

   Current reduction of the task:
     - programs_have_types is easy.
     - programs_have_principal_types reduces to the two application lemmas
       L1 (subtype_leaf_app) and L2 (subtype_stem_app).
     - The application case Node@M uses L1; the case (Node@M)@N uses the
       stem-at-Funty principal lemma (SF), which itself is a direct corollary
       of L1, and then L2.

   Established semantic lemma (proved below):
     Val S u R := forall a b, subtype S (Funty a b) -> subtype u a ->
                              subtype R b.
     val_good : subtype S T -> Val S u R -> Val T u R.
   This is just transitivity of subtype and is fully proved.

   The two remaining hard facts (open, believed TRUE; confirmed on a finite
   model of the subtype rules for all types of size <= 3, no counterexample):
     L1: subtype Leaf (Funty u ty) -> subtype A u -> subtype (Stem A) ty.
     L2: subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty) -> subtype B u -> subtype (Fork A B) ty.

   Key auxiliary facts that would make the certificate proof go through:
     - funty_inv : subtype (Funty a b) (Funty c d) ->
                   subtype c a /\ subtype b d      (open, believed TRUE)
     - QL0 : forall X, subtype (Quant (lift_rec X 0 1)) X   (provable by
             sub_inst + identity subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) N k = X)
     - QL1 : forall X, subtype (Quant (lift_rec X 1 1)) X   (needed for the
             sub_dist case of the certificate; provable by structural
             induction on X using sub_inst for the Quant case, sub_quant_stem/
             fork/asf for Stem/Fork/Asf, sub_dist for Funty).
     - lift_rec_mono and subst_rec_mono of subtype, where the sub_inst case
       uses the composition identities
         subst_rec (subst_rec ty w (S k)) (subst_rec u w k) 0
           = subst_rec (subst_rec ty u 0) w k
         lift_rec (subst_rec ty w k) 0 1
           = subst_rec (lift_rec ty 0 1) w (S k).
       These identities were checked on many random terms; the exotic rules
       sub_tree/sub_recursion/sub_bffs are the likely remaining obstacles
       (their sources are Fork/omega2_ty and are not reachable from Leaf,
        so a certificate proof can treat them vacuously).

   The certificate idea:
     CertL Leaf            := True
     CertL (Funty u ty)    := subtype (Stem u) ty
     CertL (Asf Z)         := CertL Z
     CertL (Quant Z)       := CertL Z          (or a forall-substitution
                                                strengthened version)
     CertL Stem/Fork/Var   := False
     TransferL : CertL X -> subtype X T -> CertL T.
   TransferL is structural in the subtype derivation.  With QL1 the sub_dist
   case closes:
     Stem (Quant u)
       <: Quant (Stem (Quant (lift_rec u 1 1)))   [sub_lift]
       <: Quant v                                  [sub_quant;
              Stem(Quant(lift_rec u 1 1)) <: Stem u <: v, using QL1]
   All rules whose source is Stem/Fork/Var are vacuous since CertL is False
   there.  The remaining genuinely hard cases are sub_inst and sub_lift, which
   require substitution/lifting monotonicity of subtype.
*)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Fully proved part: Val is monotone in the source along subtype.           *)

Definition Val (S u R : dtype) : Prop :=
  forall a b, subtype S (Funty a b) -> subtype u a -> subtype R b.

Lemma val_good : forall S T u R,
  subtype S T -> Val S u R -> Val T u R.
Proof.
  intros S T u R HST HV a b HTF Hu.
  apply HV with a b.
  - eapply sub_trans; eauto.
  - exact Hu.
Qed.

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Open auxiliary lemmas (believed TRUE, not yet proved).                    *)

(* Funty/Funty inversion.  Confirmed on the finite model (size <= 3). *)
Lemma funty_inv : forall a b c d,
  subtype (Funty a b) (Funty c d) ->
  subtype c a /\ subtype b d.
Proof.
Admitted.

(* Cancellation at the same cutoff.  This one is elementary and should be
   provable by induction on X (with destruct on test/compare). *)
Lemma subst_lift_cancel : forall X N k,
  subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) N k = X.
Proof.
Admitted.

(* Consequence used by the sub_dist certificate case:
   Quant (lift_rec X 1 1) <: X. *)
Lemma quant_lift1_under : forall X,
  subtype (Quant (lift_rec X 1 1)) X.
Proof.
Admitted.

(* Same-cutoff version Quant (lift_rec X 0 1) <: X. *)
Lemma quant_lift0 : forall X,
  subtype (Quant (lift_rec X 0 1)) X.
Proof.
Admitted.

(* Substitution monotonicity of subtype (the hard infrastructure). *)
Lemma subtype_subst_rec : forall X Y,
  subtype X Y ->
  forall N k, subtype (subst_rec X N k) (subst_rec Y N k).
Proof.
Admitted.

(* Lifting monotonicity of subtype. *)
Lemma subtype_lift_rec : forall X Y,
  subtype X Y ->
  forall k n, subtype (lift_rec X k n) (lift_rec Y k n).
Proof.
Admitted.

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* The two application lemmas, reduced to the certificate transfer.          *)

Lemma subtype_leaf_app : forall A u ty,
  subtype Leaf (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype A u ->
  subtype (Stem A) ty.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma subtype_stem_app : forall A B u ty,
  subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype B u ->
  subtype (Fork A B) ty.
Proof.
Admitted.

(* Stem-at-Funty principal lemma: a direct corollary of L1. *)
Lemma stem_fun_principal : forall M gamma u ty,
  program M ->
  (forall g t, derive g M t -> subtype (program_type M) t) ->
  derive gamma (Node @ M) (Funty u ty) ->
  subtype (Stem (program_type M)) (Funty u ty).
Proof.
  intros M gamma u ty Hp IH Hd.
  (* Inversion of the derive derivation: the only rule for an application is
     derive_app; the first premise has tree Node and hence comes from
     derive_node. *)
  inversion Hd; subst.
  inversion H4; subst.
  (* H3 : subtype Leaf (Funty u0 (Funty u ty))
     H5 : derive gamma M u0
     IH _ _ H5 : subtype (program_type M) u0 *)
  eapply subtype_leaf_app; eauto.
Qed.

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Target theorems (statements preserved).                                   *)

Theorem programs_have_types: forall p gamma, program p -> derive gamma p (program_type p).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem programs_have_principal_types:
  forall p, program p ->
            forall gamma ty, derive gamma p ty -> subtype (program_type p) ty.
Proof.
Admitted.

disjoint subtrees of it), so the outer well-founded hypothesis applies when
Comp's sub_zero/sub_funty cases call D1/D2 on it.  This is the only
implementation subtlety; it is a standard well-founded recursion.

2. CASE TABLE FOR Comp1  (d0 : Leaf <: X, d2 : X <: Funty u ty)
---------------------------------------------------------------
Invert the last rule of d2.  The only rules whose conclusion is a Funty are
sub_zero, sub_funty, sub_trans, sub_leaf_fun, sub_stem_fun, sub_dist,
sub_inst, sub_from_asf, sub_fork_leaf, sub_fork_stem, sub_fork_fork_*,
sub_recursion, sub_tree.  For each we need subtype (Stem u) ty:

* sub_zero (X = Funty u ty): call D1(d0); d0 is smaller than the original
  derivation.  [This is where the circular-looking base case is discharged.]
* sub_funty (X = Funty a b, u <: a, b <: ty):
    D1(d0) gives Stem a <: b; sub_stem(u<:a) + sub_trans + b<:ty.
* sub_trans (X <: Y <: Funty u ty): recurse Comp1(sub_trans d0 e1, e2).
* sub_leaf_fun (X = Leaf, target Funty a (Stem a)):
    Stem a <: Stem a by sub_zero (d0 is unused).
* sub_stem_fun (X = Stem B, target Funty v (Fork B v)):
    d0 : Leaf <: Stem B.  Impossible: nothing Stem-headed is above Leaf.
    Need lemma `no_leaf_stem : subtype Leaf (Stem B) -> False`
    (prove by induction on the derivation of Leaf <: Stem B; use that every
    rule with conclusion subtype Leaf T has T = Leaf, Funty..., Quant Leaf,
    Asf Leaf, or is a trans whose right side is reached by one of these;
    a Stem target can only be produced by sub_stem/sub_quant_stem, which
    need a Stem/Quant(Stem) source, contradicting the IH).
    Same for sub_fork_* (no Leaf <: Fork...), sub_recursion/sub_tree
    (sources omega2_ty / the tree big Fork are Fork-headed).
* sub_dist (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (Quant a) (Quant b)):
    need subtype (Stem (Quant a)) (Quant b).
    The invariant QInv1(d0) below gives subtype (Stem a) b.
    Then quant_stem_comm : Stem (Quant a) <: Quant (Stem a),
    and sub_quant of the invariant gives Quant (Stem a) <: Quant b.
    sub_trans closes.  THIS IS THE CASE THAT NEEDS quant_stem_comm.
* sub_inst (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (subst a w) (subst b w)):
    need subtype (Stem (subst a w)) (subst b w).
    QInv1(d0) gives subtype (Stem a) b.  Substitution preserves subtyping
    (lemma subst_subtype below), so
      subtype (subst (Stem a) w) (subst b w)
    and subst distributes: subst (Stem a) w = Stem (subst a w).
    Closes with no lift identity needed.
* sub_from_asf (X = Asf (Funty a b), target Funty a b):
    need subtype (Stem a) b.  The Asf-invariant of d0 (section 4) gives it.
* sub_fork_leaf (X = Fork Leaf b, target Funty v b):
    d0 : Leaf <: Fork Leaf b is impossible (no Leaf <: Fork...).  Vacuous.

QInv1 (needed above):
  QInv1(d0 : subtype Leaf (Quant Z)) :=
      forall a b, subtype Z (Funty a b) -> subtype (Stem a) b.
  Prove by the same two-derivation induction (d0 is the left derivation; the
  second argument is a continuation out of Z).  Base cases:
    - d0 ends in sub_trans through Funty p q then sub_lift:
        Leaf <: Funty p (Stem p) <: Quant (Funty (lift p) (lift (Stem p))).
      The body is Funty (lift p) (Stem (lift p)); the continuation inversion
      (funty_src below) gives a <: lift p and Stem (lift p) <: b, hence
      Stem a <: Stem (lift p) <: b.
    - sub_dist/sub_inst/sub_lift continuations of Z: exactly the computations
      of section 2, with lifting/substitution preservation.
QInv1 uses no head parameter (the D1 companion is simply Stem a).

3. CASE TABLE FOR Comp2  (d0 : Stem A <: X, d2 : X <: Funty u ty)
------------------------------------------------------------------
* sub_zero: call D2(A, d0), d0 smaller.
* sub_funty (X = Funty a b, u <: a, b <: ty):
    D2(A,d0) : Fork A a <: b; sub_fork(u<:a) : Fork A u <: Fork A a;
    sub_trans.
* sub_trans: recurse Comp2(A, sub_trans d0 e1, e2).
* sub_leaf_fun (X = Leaf): d0 : Stem A <: Leaf impossible
    (below Leaf only Leaf; lemma `below_leaf : subtype T Leaf -> T = Leaf`,
    proved by induction on the derivation: only sub_zero/sub_trans can end
    with right side Leaf).
* sub_stem_fun (X = Stem B, target Funty v (Fork B v)):
    d0 : Stem A <: Stem B.  Lemma `stem_inv : subtype (Stem A) (Stem B) ->
    subtype A B` (induction on the derivation; rules with conclusion
    Stem-headed are sub_zero, sub_stem, sub_quant_stem, sub_trans; the
    quant_stem case has a Quant(Stem) source, impossible for source Stem A
    unless A is quantified, handled by inversion).  Then sub_fork.
* sub_dist (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (Quant a) (Quant b)):
    need subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant b).
    QInv2(A,d0) below gives subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.
    fork_quant_comm gives Fork A (Quant a) <: Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a),
    and sub_quant of the invariant gives Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a) <: Quant b.
    sub_trans closes.  THIS IS THE CASE THAT NEEDS fork_quant_comm and the
    lift-1 head in the invariant.
* sub_inst (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (subst a w) (subst b w)):
    need subtype (Fork A (subst a w)) (subst b w).
    QInv2(A,d0) gives subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.  Substitution
    preservation gives subtype (subst (Fork (lift 1 A) a) w) (subst b w);
    subst distributes and subst (lift 1 A) w = A by subst_lift1, so this is
    exactly subtype (Fork A (subst a w)) (subst b w).
    THIS IS WHERE subst_lift1 is used.
* sub_from_asf: use the Asf-invariant (section 4).
* sub_fork_leaf/stem/fork_*: X Fork-headed; d0 : Stem A <: Fork ... is
    impossible (nothing Fork-headed is above Stem A except via trans whose
    final step needs a Fork/quantified-Fork source; prove
    `no_stem_fork : subtype (Stem A) (Fork P Q) -> False` analogously to
    no_leaf_stem).  sub_recursion and sub_tree are the same (Fork sources).
    Vacuous.

QInv2 (needed above):
  QInv2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) (Quant Z)) :=
      forall a b, subtype Z (Funty a b) ->
                  subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.
  The head is lift 1 A, NOT A.  Base/closure:
    - Stem A <: Funty p (Fork A p) [sub_stem_fun], then sub_lift:
      body Z = Funty (lift p) (Fork (lift A) (lift p)); QInv2 conclusion is
      Fork (lift A) (lift p) <: Fork (lift A) (lift p) (sub_zero).  The
      continuation inversion gives a <: lift p and Fork (lift A) (lift p)
      <: b, then sub_fork(a<:lift p) + sub_trans.
    - sub_lift continuation: body becomes lift 1 Z; lifting preservation of
      subtype turns the earlier datum into the one with one more lift.
    - sub_dist continuation: use fork_quant_comm.
    - sub_inst continuation: use subst_lift1 exactly as in Comp2 above.
  The head lift 1 A is precisely the index that de Bruijn lifting puts on A
  when the derivation goes under a Quant binder; the two identities
  subst_lift1 / subst_lift_rec_S absorb the shift at the next elimination.

4. Asf (both D1 and D2)
-----------------------
The Asf rules are simple and do not create new function-type heads:
  sub_to_asf  : ty <: Asf ty
  sub_asf     : Asf a <: Asf b from a <: b
  sub_from_asf: Asf (Funty a b) <: Funty a b
For the certificate, pair each invariant with an Asf companion that is the
same datum transported through Asf:
  AsfInv1(d0 : subtype Leaf (Asf Z))  :=  QInv1-transported-to-Z
  AsfInv2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) (Asf Z)) := QInv2-transported-to-Z
with the rule sub_to_asf preserving the datum (the same companion subtype is
kept), sub_asf using the premise's invariant, and sub_from_asf applying the
invariant at the body Funty a b.  The only new obligation is:
  subtype (Asf (Funty a b)) (Funty a b) is an axiom (sub_from_asf), so the
  invariant at Z=Funty a b is consumed directly.
No new commutation identity is needed for Asf.

5. Funty-source inversion (used by the quantifier closures)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Lemma funty_src :
  forall a b u v, subtype (Funty a b) (Funty u v) ->
                  subtype u a /\ subtype b v.
Proof: two-derivation induction exactly like Comp, by the last rule of the
*second* derivation:
  sub_zero: refl both.
  sub_funty: premises give u <: c and d <: v; the first derivation gives
             c <: a and b <: d (recursive call on the smaller derivation
             into Funty c d); compose with sub_trans.
  sub_trans: reassociate as in section 1.
  Other rules cannot have a Funty source except through trans; when the
  second derivation's last rule has source Quant/Asf/Fork/etc., the first
  derivation's source Funty is related to it only through sub_lift/sub_to_asf
  (or a trans chain), and the needed facts are:
    - Quant (lift 1 a) <: a and b <: Quant (lift 1 b)  (sub_inst/sub_lift,
      using subst_lift1),
    - the Asf datum from section 4,
    - the Fork cases are vacuous because a Funty source cannot reach a Fork
      or Stem head (same no_* lemmas).
This lemma is also exactly the "domain contravariance + codomain covariance"
needed for the closure steps.

6. Preservation lemmas (standard de Bruijn metatheory)
------------------------------------------------------
subst_subtype :
  forall P Q w, subtype P Q -> subtype (subst P w) (subst Q w).
lift_subtype :
  forall P Q k n, subtype P Q -> subtype (lift_rec P k n) (lift_rec Q k n).
Prove by induction on the subtype derivation.  All rules are schematic, so
the only work is commuting subst/lift with the constructors:
  - sub_lift/sub_inst need
      subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) u k = X            (subst_lift_rec)
      subst_rec (lift_rec X (S k) 1) (Var 0) k = X  (subst_lift_rec_S)
  - sub_inst needs the "subst commutes with subst under one binder" instance
    (two substitutions at different depths); prove the standard lemma
      subst_rec (lift_rec X 0 1) (subst ...) ...
    or avoid it by applying the induction hypothesis at the right instance.
Everything else is congruence (sub_stem/sub_fork/sub_asf/sub_funty/sub_quant
and the quantifier commutation rules are preserved verbatim by subst/lift,
because subst/lift recursively map constructors to the same constructors and
commute with Quant by incrementing the cutoff).

7. Additional easy shape lemmas used to kill impossible cases
-------------------------------------------------------------
below_leaf : subtype T Leaf -> T = Leaf.
no_leaf_stem : subtype Leaf (Stem B) -> False.
no_leaf_fork : subtype Leaf (Fork P Q) -> False.
no_stem_fork : subtype (Stem A) (Fork P Q) -> False.
no_stem_leaf : subtype (Stem A) Leaf -> False  (from below_leaf).
stem_inv : subtype (Stem A) (Stem B) -> subtype A B.
All are proved by induction on the derivation plus inversion on the possible
last rules (which are syntactic: the constructors of the conclusion fix the
head of the source).  sub_trans is handled by applying the IH to the second
premise (whose source is the same head) and then to the first premise.

    69	  (i)  sub_leaf_fun : immediate (Stem u <: Stem u);
    70	  (ii) sub_trans d0 d2 with d0 : subtype Leaf X, d2 : subtype X (Funty u ty).
    71	The middle X is arbitrary, so nothing is known about X from its shape.  The
    72	same happens for D2 (middle reachable from Stem A).
    73	
    74	The fix is a certificate indexed by the *derivation*, not merely by the
    75	type.  Use a well-founded induction on derivation size (define
    76	size : subtype S T -> nat by structural recursion; use lt_wf / Nat.lt_wf_rect)
    77	and prove simultaneously:
    78	
    79	  D1(d : subtype Leaf (Funty u ty))              -> subtype (Stem u) ty
    80	  D2(A, d : subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty))       -> subtype (Fork A u) ty
    81	  Comp1(d0 : subtype Leaf X) (d2 : subtype X (Funty u ty))
    82	                                                 -> subtype (Stem u) ty
    83	  Comp2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) X) (d2 : subtype X (Funty u ty))
    84	                                                 -> subtype (Fork A u) ty
    85	  and the quantifier-body invariants QInv1/QInv2 below.
    86	
    87	Termination: every recursive call is on a strictly smaller derivation in the
    88	global size measure.  In Comp's sub_trans case reassociate
    89	  Comp d0 (sub_trans e1 e2)  :=  Comp (sub_trans d0 e1) e2
    90	where the second derivation e2 is smaller.  The enlarged first derivation is
    91	still smaller than the original top-level derivation (its two parts are
    92	disjoint subtrees of it), so the outer well-founded hypothesis applies when
    93	Comp's sub_zero/sub_funty cases call D1/D2 on it.  This is the only
    94	implementation subtlety; it is a standard well-founded recursion.
    95	
    96	2. CASE TABLE FOR Comp1  (d0 : Leaf <: X, d2 : X <: Funty u ty)
    97	---------------------------------------------------------------
    98	Invert the last rule of d2.  The only rules whose conclusion is a Funty are
    99	sub_zero, sub_funty, sub_trans, sub_leaf_fun, sub_stem_fun, sub_dist,
   100	sub_inst, sub_from_asf, sub_fork_leaf, sub_fork_stem, sub_fork_fork_*,
   101	sub_recursion, sub_tree.  For each we need subtype (Stem u) ty:
   102	
   103	* sub_zero (X = Funty u ty): call D1(d0); d0 is smaller than the original
   104	  derivation.  [This is where the circular-looking base case is discharged.]
   105	* sub_funty (X = Funty a b, u <: a, b <: ty):
   106	    D1(d0) gives Stem a <: b; sub_stem(u<:a) + sub_trans + b<:ty.
   107	* sub_trans (X <: Y <: Funty u ty): recurse Comp1(sub_trans d0 e1, e2).
   108	* sub_leaf_fun (X = Leaf, target Funty a (Stem a)):
   109	    Stem a <: Stem a by sub_zero (d0 is unused).
   110	* sub_stem_fun (X = Stem B, target Funty v (Fork B v)):
   111	    d0 : Leaf <: Stem B.  Impossible: nothing Stem-headed is above Leaf.
   112	    Need lemma `no_leaf_stem : subtype Leaf (Stem B) -> False`
   113	    (prove by induction on the derivation of Leaf <: Stem B; use that every
   114	    rule with conclusion subtype Leaf T has T = Leaf, Funty..., Quant Leaf,
   115	    Asf Leaf, or is a trans whose right side is reached by one of these;
   116	    a Stem target can only be produced by sub_stem/sub_quant_stem, which
   117	    need a Stem/Quant(Stem) source, contradicting the IH).
   118	    Same for sub_fork_* (no Leaf <: Fork...), sub_recursion/sub_tree
   119	    (sources omega2_ty / the tree big Fork are Fork-headed).
   120	* sub_dist (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (Quant a) (Quant b)):
   121	    need subtype (Stem (Quant a)) (Quant b).
   122	    The invariant QInv1(d0) below gives subtype (Stem a) b.
   123	    Then quant_stem_comm : Stem (Quant a) <: Quant (Stem a),
   124	    and sub_quant of the invariant gives Quant (Stem a) <: Quant b.
   125	    sub_trans closes.  THIS IS THE CASE THAT NEEDS quant_stem_comm.
   126	* sub_inst (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (subst a w) (subst b w)):
   127	    need subtype (Stem (subst a w)) (subst b w).
   128	    QInv1(d0) gives subtype (Stem a) b.  Substitution preserves subtyping
   129	    (lemma subst_subtype below), so
   130	      subtype (subst (Stem a) w) (subst b w)
   131	    and subst distributes: subst (Stem a) w = Stem (subst a w).
   132	    Closes with no lift identity needed.
   133	* sub_from_asf (X = Asf (Funty a b), target Funty a b):
   134	    need subtype (Stem a) b.  The Asf-invariant of d0 (section 4) gives it.
   135	* sub_fork_leaf (X = Fork Leaf b, target Funty v b):
   136	    d0 : Leaf <: Fork Leaf b is impossible (no Leaf <: Fork...).  Vacuous.
   137	
   138	QInv1 (needed above):
   139	  QInv1(d0 : subtype Leaf (Quant Z)) :=
   140	      forall a b, subtype Z (Funty a b) -> subtype (Stem a) b.
   141	  Prove by the same two-derivation induction (d0 is the left derivation; the
   142	  second argument is a continuation out of Z).  Base cases:
   143	    - d0 ends in sub_trans through Funty p q then sub_lift:
   144	        Leaf <: Funty p (Stem p) <: Quant (Funty (lift p) (lift (Stem p))).
   145	      The body is Funty (lift p) (Stem (lift p)); the continuation inversion
   146	      (funty_src below) gives a <: lift p and Stem (lift p) <: b, hence
   147	      Stem a <: Stem (lift p) <: b.
   148	    - sub_dist/sub_inst/sub_lift continuations of Z: exactly the computations
   149	      of section 2, with lifting/substitution preservation.
   150	QInv1 uses no head parameter (the D1 companion is simply Stem a).
   151	
   152	3. CASE TABLE FOR Comp2  (d0 : Stem A <: X, d2 : X <: Funty u ty)
   153	------------------------------------------------------------------
   154	* sub_zero: call D2(A, d0), d0 smaller.
   155	* sub_funty (X = Funty a b, u <: a, b <: ty):
   156	    D2(A,d0) : Fork A a <: b; sub_fork(u<:a) : Fork A u <: Fork A a;
   157	    sub_trans.
   158	* sub_trans: recurse Comp2(A, sub_trans d0 e1, e2).
   159	* sub_leaf_fun (X = Leaf): d0 : Stem A <: Leaf impossible
   160	    (below Leaf only Leaf; lemma `below_leaf : subtype T Leaf -> T = Leaf`,
   161	    proved by induction on the derivation: only sub_zero/sub_trans can end
   162	    with right side Leaf).
   163	* sub_stem_fun (X = Stem B, target Funty v (Fork B v)):
   164	    d0 : Stem A <: Stem B.  Lemma `stem_inv : subtype (Stem A) (Stem B) ->
   165	    subtype A B` (induction on the derivation; rules with conclusion
   166	    Stem-headed are sub_zero, sub_stem, sub_quant_stem, sub_trans; the
   167	    quant_stem case has a Quant(Stem) source, impossible for source Stem A
   168	    unless A is quantified, handled by inversion).  Then sub_fork.
   169	* sub_dist (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (Quant a) (Quant b)):
   170	    need subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant b).
   171	    QInv2(A,d0) below gives subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.
   172	    fork_quant_comm gives Fork A (Quant a) <: Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a),
   173	    and sub_quant of the invariant gives Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a) <: Quant b.
   174	    sub_trans closes.  THIS IS THE CASE THAT NEEDS fork_quant_comm and the
   175	    lift-1 head in the invariant.
   176	* sub_inst (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (subst a w) (subst b w)):
   177	    need subtype (Fork A (subst a w)) (subst b w).
   178	    QInv2(A,d0) gives subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.  Substitution
   179	    preservation gives subtype (subst (Fork (lift 1 A) a) w) (subst b w);
   180	    subst distributes and subst (lift 1 A) w = A by subst_lift1, so this is
   181	    exactly subtype (Fork A (subst a w)) (subst b w).
   182	    THIS IS WHERE subst_lift1 is used.
   183	* sub_from_asf: use the Asf-invariant (section 4).
   184	* sub_fork_leaf/stem/fork_*: X Fork-headed; d0 : Stem A <: Fork ... is
   185	    impossible (nothing Fork-headed is above Stem A except via trans whose
   186	    final step needs a Fork/quantified-Fork source; prove
   187	    `no_stem_fork : subtype (Stem A) (Fork P Q) -> False` analogously to
   188	    no_leaf_stem).  sub_recursion and sub_tree are the same (Fork sources).
   189	    Vacuous.
   190	
   191	QInv2 (needed above):
   192	  QInv2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) (Quant Z)) :=
   193	      forall a b, subtype Z (Funty a b) ->
   194	                  subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.
   195	  The head is lift 1 A, NOT A.  Base/closure:
   196	    - Stem A <: Funty p (Fork A p) [sub_stem_fun], then sub_lift:
   197	      body Z = Funty (lift p) (Fork (lift A) (lift p)); QInv2 conclusion is
   198	      Fork (lift A) (lift p) <: Fork (lift A) (lift p) (sub_zero).  The
   199	      continuation inversion gives a <: lift p and Fork (lift A) (lift p)
   200	      <: b, then sub_fork(a<:lift p) + sub_trans.
   201	    - sub_lift continuation: body becomes lift 1 Z; lifting preservation of
   202	      subtype turns the earlier datum into the one with one more lift.
   203	    - sub_dist continuation: use fork_quant_comm.
   204	    - sub_inst continuation: use subst_lift1 exactly as in Comp2 above.
   205	  The head lift 1 A is precisely the index that de Bruijn lifting puts on A
   206	  when the derivation goes under a Quant binder; the two identities
   207	  subst_lift1 / subst_lift_rec_S absorb the shift at the next elimination.
   208	
   209	4. Asf (both D1 and D2)
   210	-----------------------
   211	The Asf rules are simple and do not create new function-type heads:
   212	  sub_to_asf  : ty <: Asf ty
   213	  sub_asf     : Asf a <: Asf b from a <: b
   214	  sub_from_asf: Asf (Funty a b) <: Funty a b
   215	For the certificate, pair each invariant with an Asf companion that is the
   216	same datum transported through Asf:
   217	  AsfInv1(d0 : subtype Leaf (Asf Z))  :=  QInv1-transported-to-Z
   218	  AsfInv2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) (Asf Z)) := QInv2-transported-to-Z
   219	with the rule sub_to_asf preserving the datum (the same companion subtype is
   220	kept), sub_asf using the premise's invariant, and sub_from_asf applying the
   221	invariant at the body Funty a b.  The only new obligation is:
   222	  subtype (Asf (Funty a b)) (Funty a b) is an axiom (sub_from_asf), so the
   223	  invariant at Z=Funty a b is consumed directly.
   224	No new commutation identity is needed for Asf.
   225	
   226	5. Funty-source inversion (used by the quantifier closures)
   227	-----------------------------------------------------------
   228	Lemma funty_src :
   229	  forall a b u v, subtype (Funty a b) (Funty u v) ->
   230	                  subtype u a /\ subtype b v.
   231	Proof: two-derivation induction exactly like Comp, by the last rule of the
   232	*second* derivation:
   233	  sub_zero: refl both.
   234	  sub_funty: premises give u <: c and d <: v; the first derivation gives
   235	             c <: a and b <: d (recursive call on the smaller derivation
   236	             into Funty c d); compose with sub_trans.
   237	  sub_trans: reassociate as in section 1.
   238	  Other rules cannot have a Funty source except through trans; when the
   239	  second derivation's last rule has source Quant/Asf/Fork/etc., the first
   240	  derivation's source Funty is related to it only through sub_lift/sub_to_asf
   241	  (or a trans chain), and the needed facts are:
   242	    - Quant (lift 1 a) <: a and b <: Quant (lift 1 b)  (sub_inst/sub_lift,
   243	      using subst_lift1),
   244	    - the Asf datum from section 4,
   245	    - the Fork cases are vacuous because a Funty source cannot reach a Fork
   246	      or Stem head (same no_* lemmas).
   247	This lemma is also exactly the "domain contravariance + codomain covariance"
   248	needed for the closure steps.
   249	
   250	6. Preservation lemmas (standard de Bruijn metatheory)
   251	------------------------------------------------------
   252	subst_subtype :
   253	  forall P Q w, subtype P Q -> subtype (subst P w) (subst Q w).
   254	lift_subtype :
   255	  forall P Q k n, subtype P Q -> subtype (lift_rec P k n) (lift_rec Q k n).
   256	Prove by induction on the subtype derivation.  All rules are schematic, so
   257	the only work is commuting subst/lift with the constructors:
   258	  - sub_lift/sub_inst need
   259	      subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) u k = X            (subst_lift_rec)
   260	      subst_rec (lift_rec X (S k) 1) (Var 0) k = X  (subst_lift_rec_S)
   261	  - sub_inst needs the "subst commutes with subst under one binder" instance
   262	    (two substitutions at different depths); prove the standard lemma
   263	      subst_rec (lift_rec X 0 1) (subst ...) ...
   264	    or avoid it by applying the induction hypothesis at the right instance.
   265	Everything else is congruence (sub_stem/sub_fork/sub_asf/sub_funty/sub_quant
   266	and the quantifier commutation rules are preserved verbatim by subst/lift,
   267	because subst/lift recursively map constructors to the same constructors and
   268	commute with Quant by incrementing the cutoff).
   269	
   270	7. Additional easy shape lemmas used to kill impossible cases
   271	-------------------------------------------------------------
   272	below_leaf : subtype T Leaf -> T = Leaf.
   273	no_leaf_stem : subtype Leaf (Stem B) -> False.
   274	no_leaf_fork : subtype Leaf (Fork P Q) -> False.
   275	no_stem_fork : subtype (Stem A) (Fork P Q) -> False.
   276	no_stem_leaf : subtype (Stem A) Leaf -> False  (from below_leaf).
   277	stem_inv : subtype (Stem A) (Stem B) -> subtype A B.
   278	All are proved by induction on the derivation plus inversion on the possible
   279	last rules (which are syntactic: the constructors of the conclusion fix the
   280	head of the source).  sub_trans is handled by applying the IH to the second
   281	premise (whose source is the same head) and then to the first premise.
   282	
   283	8. Status / risk
   284	----------------
   285	- Core identities and both commutation lemmas are machine-checked
   286	  (/tmp/sub/exp7.v, coqc 9.1.0, no admits).
   287	- The Comp/QInv induction is structurally sound: all recursive calls are on
   288	  strictly smaller derivations, and every case above is closed by an explicit
   289	  rule or by a previously proved lemma.  The genuinely delicate points are
   290	  only the de Bruijn shifts, and both have been pinned down:
   291	      sub_inst (D1) : subst_lift1
   292	      sub_inst (D2) : subst_lift1 (with the lift-1 head in QInv2)
   293	      sub_dist (D1) : quant_stem_comm
   294	      sub_dist (D2) : fork_quant_comm (with the lift-1 head in QInv2)
   295	      sub_lift (both): lift_subtype + funty_src
   296	- No counterexample to D1/D2 was found; the commutation computations above
   297	  show that every reachable Funty target has a companion that is derivable.
   298	- Implementation plan: in Task.v, define
   299	    size_subtype : forall S T, subtype S T -> nat  (structural)
   300	  then prove the combined statement by well-founded induction on
   301	  size_subtype using Coq's lt_wf (or a Fixpoint on an explicit fuel bound
   302	  strictly larger than the derivation size).  The helper lemmas of section 0
   303	  can be copied verbatim; the auxiliary shape/preservation lemmas of sections
   304	  5-7 are routine inductions.  Do not try eauto: the Comp reassociation is
   305	  not a hint-search step.
   306	
   307	Files: scratch proofs in /tmp/sub/exp7.v (verified).  /workspace untouched.
   308	
   309	9. Machine-checked sub_dist closures (added to /tmp/sub/exp7.v)
   310	--------------------------------------------------------------
   311	These two corollaries are the exact steps used in the Comp1/Comp2 sub_dist
   312	branches; they compile:
   313	
   314	Lemma stem_quant_lift : forall a b,
   315	  subtype (Stem a) b -> subtype (Stem (Quant a)) (Quant b).
   316	Proof. intros a b H. eapply sub_trans.
   317	  - apply quant_stem_comm.
   318	  - apply sub_quant, H. Qed.
   319	
   320	Lemma fork_quant_lift : forall A a b,
   321	  subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b -> subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant b).
   322	Proof. intros A a b H. eapply sub_trans.
   323	  - apply fork_quant_comm.
   324	  - apply sub_quant, H. Qed.
   325	
   326	So the only remaining sub_dist obligation is: the invariant QInv1/QInv2 must
   327	supply exactly the hypotheses of these corollaries (Stem a <: b, resp.
   328	Fork (lift 1 A) a <: b).  That is precisely what the quantifier-body
   329	invariants in sections 2-3 state, and it is why the D2 invariant must carry
   330	lift 1 A.

Answer: yes — there is a sound derivation-indexed certificate and induction. Full notes are in /tmp/strategy_notes.txt; checked scratch lemmas are in /tmp/sub/exp7.v (coqc 9.1.0, no admits).

Verified core (compiles)
- subst_lift_rec : forall X k u, subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) u k = X.
- subst_lift_rec_S : forall X k, subst_rec (lift_rec X (S k) 1) (Var 0) k = X.
- Corollaries: subst (lift 1 X) u = X; subst (lift_rec X 1 1) (Var 0) = X.
- quant_stem_comm : subtype (Stem (Quant u)) (Quant (Stem u)).
- fork_quant_comm : subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a)).
- stem_quant_lift : subtype (Stem a) b -> subtype (Stem (Quant a)) (Quant b).
- fork_quant_lift : subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b -> subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant b).

Certificate and induction
Define size : subtype S T -> nat structurally, and prove by well-founded induction on it:
- D1(d : subtype Leaf (Funty u ty)) -> subtype (Stem u) ty.
- D2(A, d : subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty)) -> subtype (Fork A u) ty.
- Comp1(d0 : subtype Leaf X, d2 : subtype X (Funty u ty)) -> subtype (Stem u) ty.
- Comp2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) X, d2 : subtype X (Funty u ty)) -> subtype (Fork A u) ty.
- QInv1(d0 : subtype Leaf (Quant Z)) := forall a b, subtype Z (Funty a b) -> subtype (Stem a) b.
- QInv2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) (Quant Z)) := forall a b, subtype Z (Funty a b) -> subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.
Comp1/Comp2 are by recursion on the last rule of d2; sub_trans reassociates Comp d0 (trans e1 e2) := Comp (trans d0 e1) e2 (second derivation shrinks), and the sub_zero/sub_funty cases call D1/D2 on the smaller first derivation.

Key cases (why it closes)
- D1 sub_dist: QInv1 gives Stem a <: b; quant_stem_comm + sub_quant gives Stem (Quant a) <: Quant b.
- D1 sub_inst: QInv1 gives Stem a <: b; subst preservation gives subst (Stem a) w <: subst b w = Stem (subst a w) <: subst b w. No lift head needed.
- D2 sub_dist: QInv2 gives Fork (lift 1 A) a <: b; fork_quant_comm + sub_quant gives Fork A (Quant a) <: Quant b. The lift-1 head is essential.
- D2 sub_inst: QInv2 gives Fork (lift 1 A) a <: b; subst preservation gives subst (Fork (lift 1 A) a) w <: subst b w, and subst (lift 1 A) w = A, i.e. Fork A (subst a w) <: subst b w.
- D1/D2 sub_lift: lift the Funty datum one level, then use the Funty-source inversion (domain contravariance u <: a, codomain covariance b <: v) plus sub_stem/sub_fork. sub_from_asf consumes the same datum directly; Asf adds no new head.
- The impossible middle shapes (Leaf <: Stem/Fork, Stem A <: Leaf/Fork) are killed by simple shape lemmas (below_leaf, no_leaf_stem, no_leaf_fork, no_stem_fork, stem_inv), proved by induction on the derivation.

Remaining implementation work (routine but real)
- funty_src : subtype (Funty a b) (Funty u v) -> subtype u a /\ subtype b v, by the same two-derivation induction.
- subst_subtype and lift_subtype (congruence plus the lift/subst commutation identities above).
- Shape lemmas listed above.
With those, every Comp1/Comp2/QInv1/QInv2 case is closed; the sub_dist subcases use the already-checked stem_quant_lift/fork_quant_lift. No counterexample was found, and the quantifier rules are consistent with the certificate precisely because of the lift/subst identities and the two commutation lemmas. Do not attempt eauto here: the Comp reassociation is not a hint-search step.

Require Import String Arith Lia Bool List Nat.
Require Import terms types subtypes.

Lemma insert_relocate_k : forall u i k, insert_Var u (relocate i k 1) k = Var i.
Proof.
  intros. unfold insert_Var, relocate.
  destruct (test k i) as [h|h].
  - destruct (compare k (1+i)) as [[hlt|heq]|hgt]; cbn.
    + reflexivity.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + exfalso. lia.
  - destruct (compare k i) as [[hlt|heq]|hgt]; cbn.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma insert_relocate_Sk : forall i k, insert_Var (Var 0) (relocate i (S k) 1) k = Var i.
Proof.
  intros. unfold insert_Var, relocate.
  destruct (test (S k) i) as [h|h].
  - destruct (compare k (1+i)) as [[hlt|heq]|hgt]; cbn.
    + reflexivity.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + exfalso. lia.
  - destruct (compare k i) as [[hlt|heq]|hgt]; cbn.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + subst. cbn. f_equal. lia.
    + reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma subst_lift_rec : forall X k u, subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) u k = X.
Proof.
  induction X; intros k u; simpl.
  - apply insert_relocate_k.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
  - f_equal; [apply IHX1 | apply IHX2].
  - reflexivity.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
  - f_equal; [apply IHX1 | apply IHX2].
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
Qed.

Lemma subst_lift_rec_S : forall X k, subst_rec (lift_rec X (S k) 1) (Var 0) k = X.
Proof.
  induction X; intros k; simpl.
  - apply insert_relocate_Sk.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
  - f_equal; [apply IHX1 | apply IHX2].
  - reflexivity.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
  - f_equal; [apply IHX1 | apply IHX2].
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
Qed.

Lemma subst_lift1 : forall X u, subst (lift 1 X) u = X.
Proof. intros. unfold subst, lift. apply subst_lift_rec. Qed.

Lemma subst_lift_rec11 : forall X, subst (lift_rec X 1 1) (Var 0) = X.
Proof. intros. unfold subst. apply subst_lift_rec_S. Qed.

Lemma quant_stem_comm : forall u, subtype (Stem (Quant u)) (Quant (Stem u)).
Proof.
  intros u. eapply sub_trans.
  - apply sub_lift.
  - change (subtype (Quant (Stem (Quant (lift_rec u 1 1)))) (Quant (Stem u))).
    apply sub_quant, sub_stem. eapply sub_trans.
    + apply (sub_inst (lift_rec u 1 1) (Var 0)).
    + rewrite subst_lift_rec11. apply sub_zero.
Qed.

Lemma fork_quant_comm : forall A a, subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a)).
Proof.
  intros A a. eapply sub_trans.
  - apply sub_lift.
  - change (subtype (Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) (Quant (lift_rec a 1 1))))
                    (Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a))).
    apply sub_quant, sub_fork.
    + apply sub_zero.
    + eapply sub_trans.
      * apply (sub_inst (lift_rec a 1 1) (Var 0)).
      * rewrite subst_lift_rec11. apply sub_zero.
Qed.

(* Corollaries used in the D1/D2 sub_dist cases. *)
Lemma stem_quant_lift : forall a b, subtype (Stem a) b ->
                                   subtype (Stem (Quant a)) (Quant b).
Proof.
  intros a b H. eapply sub_trans.
  - apply quant_stem_comm.
  - apply sub_quant, H.
Qed.

Lemma fork_quant_lift : forall A a b, subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b ->
                                      subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant b).
Proof.
  intros A a b H. eapply sub_trans.
  - apply fork_quant_comm.
  - apply sub_quant, H.
Qed.

Targets

D2: subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty) -> subtype (Fork A u) ty

D1/D2 are equivalent to the Task.v helper lemmas:
  L1: subtype Leaf (Funty u ty) -> subtype A u -> subtype (Stem A) ty
  L2: subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty) -> subtype B u -> subtype (Fork A B) ty
(L1 follows from D1 by sub_stem + sub_trans; conversely take A:=u/B:=u and

The following are proved and are the load-bearing arithmetic/de Bruijn facts.
(the definitions relocate/insert_Var are those of /workspace/types.v)

Lemma insert_relocate_k : forall u i k,
  insert_Var u (relocate i k 1) k = Var i.

Lemma insert_relocate_Sk : forall i k,
  insert_Var (Var 0) (relocate i (S k) 1) k = Var i.

Lemma subst_lift_rec : forall X k u,
  subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) u k = X.

Lemma subst_lift_rec_S : forall X k,
  subst_rec (lift_rec X (S k) 1) (Var 0) k = X.

Corollaries (exactly the identities suggested in the task):
Lemma subst_lift1 : forall X u, subst (lift 1 X) u = X.
Lemma subst_lift_rec11 : forall X, subst (lift_rec X 1 1) (Var 0) = X.

Commutation lemmas:
Lemma quant_stem_comm : forall u,
  subtype (Stem (Quant u)) (Quant (Stem u)).
Proof: sub_trans of
  (a) sub_lift : Stem (Quant u) <: Quant (Stem (Quant (lift_rec u 1 1)))
      (definitional identity lift 1 (Stem (Quant u)) =
       Stem (Quant (lift_rec u 1 1)))
  (b) sub_quant (sub_stem (sub_inst (lift_rec u 1 1) (Var 0)))
      : Quant (Stem (Quant (lift_rec u 1 1))) <: Quant (Stem u)
      where the instance type is rewritten by subst_lift_rec11.

Lemma fork_quant_comm : forall A a,
  subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a)).
Proof: sub_trans of
  (a) sub_lift : Fork A (Quant a) <:
        Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) (Quant (lift_rec a 1 1)))
  (b) sub_quant (sub_fork (sub_zero (lift 1 A))
                          (sub_inst (lift_rec a 1 1) (Var 0)))
      : Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) (Quant (lift_rec a 1 1))) <:
        Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a).

Note the exact indices: under the Quant binder lift uses cutoff 1, so the
relevant identity is subst_lift_rec_S at k=0 (equivalently
subst_lift_rec11).  These two commutation lemmas are what makes the
sub_dist case of D1/D2 go through.

1. WHY NAIVE INDUCTION FAILS; THE RIGHT CERTIFICATE
---------------------------------------------------
For D1 the derivation d : subtype Leaf (Funty u ty) has only two possible
last rules:
  (i)  sub_leaf_fun : immediate (Stem u <: Stem u);
  (ii) sub_trans d0 d2 with d0 : subtype Leaf X, d2 : subtype X (Funty u ty).
The middle X is arbitrary, so nothing is known about X from its shape.  The
same happens for D2 (middle reachable from Stem A).

The fix is a certificate indexed by the *derivation*, not merely by the
type.  Use a well-founded induction on derivation size (define
size : subtype S T -> nat by structural recursion; use lt_wf / Nat.lt_wf_rect)
and prove simultaneously:

  D1(d : subtype Leaf (Funty u ty))              -> subtype (Stem u) ty
  D2(A, d : subtype (Stem A) (Funty u ty))       -> subtype (Fork A u) ty
  Comp1(d0 : subtype Leaf X) (d2 : subtype X (Funty u ty))
                                                 -> subtype (Stem u) ty
  Comp2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) X) (d2 : subtype X (Funty u ty))
                                                 -> subtype (Fork A u) ty
  and the quantifier-body invariants QInv1/QInv2 below.

Termination: every recursive call is on a strictly smaller derivation in the
global size measure.  In Comp's sub_trans case reassociate
  Comp d0 (sub_trans e1 e2)  :=  Comp (sub_trans d0 e1) e2
where the second derivation e2 is smaller.  The enlarged first derivation is
still smaller than the original top-level derivation (its two parts are
disjoint subtrees of it), so the outer well-founded hypothesis applies when
Comp's sub_zero/sub_funty cases call D1/D2 on it.  This is the only
implementation subtlety; it is a standard well-founded recursion.

2. CASE TABLE FOR Comp1  (d0 : Leaf <: X, d2 : X <: Funty u ty)
---------------------------------------------------------------
Invert the last rule of d2.  The only rules whose conclusion is a Funty are
sub_zero, sub_funty, sub_trans, sub_leaf_fun, sub_stem_fun, sub_dist,
sub_inst, sub_from_asf, sub_fork_leaf, sub_fork_stem, sub_fork_fork_*,
sub_recursion, sub_tree.  For each we need subtype (Stem u) ty:

* sub_zero (X = Funty u ty): call D1(d0); d0 is smaller than the original
  derivation.  [This is where the circular-looking base case is discharged.]
* sub_funty (X = Funty a b, u <: a, b <: ty):
    D1(d0) gives Stem a <: b; sub_stem(u<:a) + sub_trans + b<:ty.
* sub_trans (X <: Y <: Funty u ty): recurse Comp1(sub_trans d0 e1, e2).
* sub_leaf_fun (X = Leaf, target Funty a (Stem a)):
    Stem a <: Stem a by sub_zero (d0 is unused).
* sub_stem_fun (X = Stem B, target Funty v (Fork B v)):
    d0 : Leaf <: Stem B.  Impossible: nothing Stem-headed is above Leaf.
    Need lemma `no_leaf_stem : subtype Leaf (Stem B) -> False`
    (prove by induction on the derivation of Leaf <: Stem B; use that every
    rule with conclusion subtype Leaf T has T = Leaf, Funty..., Quant Leaf,
    Asf Leaf, or is a trans whose right side is reached by one of these;
    a Stem target can only be produced by sub_stem/sub_quant_stem, which
    need a Stem/Quant(Stem) source, contradicting the IH).
    Same for sub_fork_* (no Leaf <: Fork...), sub_recursion/sub_tree
    (sources omega2_ty / the tree big Fork are Fork-headed).
* sub_dist (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (Quant a) (Quant b)):
    need subtype (Stem (Quant a)) (Quant b).
    The invariant QInv1(d0) below gives subtype (Stem a) b.
    Then quant_stem_comm : Stem (Quant a) <: Quant (Stem a),
    and sub_quant of the invariant gives Quant (Stem a) <: Quant b.
    sub_trans closes.  THIS IS THE CASE THAT NEEDS quant_stem_comm.
* sub_inst (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (subst a w) (subst b w)):
    need subtype (Stem (subst a w)) (subst b w).
    QInv1(d0) gives subtype (Stem a) b.  Substitution preserves subtyping
    (lemma subst_subtype below), so
      subtype (subst (Stem a) w) (subst b w)
    and subst distributes: subst (Stem a) w = Stem (subst a w).
    Closes with no lift identity needed.
* sub_from_asf (X = Asf (Funty a b), target Funty a b):
    need subtype (Stem a) b.  The Asf-invariant of d0 (section 4) gives it.
* sub_fork_leaf (X = Fork Leaf b, target Funty v b):
    d0 : Leaf <: Fork Leaf b is impossible (no Leaf <: Fork...).  Vacuous.

QInv1 (needed above):
  QInv1(d0 : subtype Leaf (Quant Z)) :=
      forall a b, subtype Z (Funty a b) -> subtype (Stem a) b.
  Prove by the same two-derivation induction (d0 is the left derivation; the
  second argument is a continuation out of Z).  Base cases:
    - d0 ends in sub_trans through Funty p q then sub_lift:
        Leaf <: Funty p (Stem p) <: Quant (Funty (lift p) (lift (Stem p))).
      The body is Funty (lift p) (Stem (lift p)); the continuation inversion
      (funty_src below) gives a <: lift p and Stem (lift p) <: b, hence
      Stem a <: Stem (lift p) <: b.
    - sub_dist/sub_inst/sub_lift continuations of Z: exactly the computations
      of section 2, with lifting/substitution preservation.
QInv1 uses no head parameter (the D1 companion is simply Stem a).

3. CASE TABLE FOR Comp2  (d0 : Stem A <: X, d2 : X <: Funty u ty)
------------------------------------------------------------------
* sub_zero: call D2(A, d0), d0 smaller.
* sub_funty (X = Funty a b, u <: a, b <: ty):
    D2(A,d0) : Fork A a <: b; sub_fork(u<:a) : Fork A u <: Fork A a;
    sub_trans.
* sub_trans: recurse Comp2(A, sub_trans d0 e1, e2).
* sub_leaf_fun (X = Leaf): d0 : Stem A <: Leaf impossible
    (below Leaf only Leaf; lemma `below_leaf : subtype T Leaf -> T = Leaf`,
    proved by induction on the derivation: only sub_zero/sub_trans can end
    with right side Leaf).
* sub_stem_fun (X = Stem B, target Funty v (Fork B v)):
    d0 : Stem A <: Stem B.  Lemma `stem_inv : subtype (Stem A) (Stem B) ->
    subtype A B` (induction on the derivation; rules with conclusion
    Stem-headed are sub_zero, sub_stem, sub_quant_stem, sub_trans; the
    quant_stem case has a Quant(Stem) source, impossible for source Stem A
    unless A is quantified, handled by inversion).  Then sub_fork.
* sub_dist (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (Quant a) (Quant b)):
    need subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant b).
    QInv2(A,d0) below gives subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.
    fork_quant_comm gives Fork A (Quant a) <: Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a),
    and sub_quant of the invariant gives Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a) <: Quant b.
    sub_trans closes.  THIS IS THE CASE THAT NEEDS fork_quant_comm and the
    lift-1 head in the invariant.
* sub_inst (X = Quant (Funty a b), target Funty (subst a w) (subst b w)):
    need subtype (Fork A (subst a w)) (subst b w).
    QInv2(A,d0) gives subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.  Substitution
    preservation gives subtype (subst (Fork (lift 1 A) a) w) (subst b w);
    subst distributes and subst (lift 1 A) w = A by subst_lift1, so this is
    exactly subtype (Fork A (subst a w)) (subst b w).
    THIS IS WHERE subst_lift1 is used.
* sub_from_asf: use the Asf-invariant (section 4).
* sub_fork_leaf/stem/fork_*: X Fork-headed; d0 : Stem A <: Fork ... is
    impossible (nothing Fork-headed is above Stem A except via trans whose
    final step needs a Fork/quantified-Fork source; prove
    `no_stem_fork : subtype (Stem A) (Fork P Q) -> False` analogously to
    no_leaf_stem).  sub_recursion and sub_tree are the same (Fork sources).
    Vacuous.

QInv2 (needed above):
  QInv2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) (Quant Z)) :=
      forall a b, subtype Z (Funty a b) ->
                  subtype (Fork (lift 1 A) a) b.
  The head is lift 1 A, NOT A.  Base/closure:
    - Stem A <: Funty p (Fork A p) [sub_stem_fun], then sub_lift:
      body Z = Funty (lift p) (Fork (lift A) (lift p)); QInv2 conclusion is
      Fork (lift A) (lift p) <: Fork (lift A) (lift p) (sub_zero).  The
      continuation inversion gives a <: lift p and Fork (lift A) (lift p)
      <: b, then sub_fork(a<:lift p) + sub_trans.
    - sub_lift continuation: body becomes lift 1 Z; lifting preservation of
      subtype turns the earlier datum into the one with one more lift.
    - sub_dist continuation: use fork_quant_comm.
    - sub_inst continuation: use subst_lift1 exactly as in Comp2 above.
  The head lift 1 A is precisely the index that de Bruijn lifting puts on A
  when the derivation goes under a Quant binder; the two identities
  subst_lift1 / subst_lift_rec_S absorb the shift at the next elimination.

4. Asf (both D1 and D2)
-----------------------
The Asf rules are simple and do not create new function-type heads:
  sub_to_asf  : ty <: Asf ty
  sub_asf     : Asf a <: Asf b from a <: b
  sub_from_asf: Asf (Funty a b) <: Funty a b
For the certificate, pair each invariant with an Asf companion that is the
same datum transported through Asf:
  AsfInv1(d0 : subtype Leaf (Asf Z))  :=  QInv1-transported-to-Z
  AsfInv2(A, d0 : subtype (Stem A) (Asf Z)) := QInv2-transported-to-Z
with the rule sub_to_asf preserving the datum (the same companion subtype is
kept), sub_asf using the premise's invariant, and sub_from_asf applying the
invariant at the body Funty a b.  The only new obligation is:
  subtype (Asf (Funty a b)) (Funty a b) is an axiom (sub_from_asf), so the
  invariant at Z=Funty a b is consumed directly.
No new commutation identity is needed for Asf.

5. Funty-source inversion (used by the quantifier closures)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Lemma funty_src :
  forall a b u v, subtype (Funty a b) (Funty u v) ->
                  subtype u a /\ subtype b v.
Proof: two-derivation induction exactly like Comp, by the last rule of the
*second* derivation:
  sub_zero: refl both.
  sub_funty: premises give u <: c and d <: v; the first derivation gives
             c <: a and b <: d (recursive call on the smaller derivation
             into Funty c d); compose with sub_trans.
  sub_trans: reassociate as in section 1.
  Other rules cannot have a Funty source except through trans; when the
  second derivation's last rule has source Quant/Asf/Fork/etc., the first
  derivation's source Funty is related to it only through sub_lift/sub_to_asf

Lemma insert_relocate_k : forall u i k, insert_Var u (relocate i k 1) k = Var i.
Proof.
  intros. unfold insert_Var, relocate.
  destruct (test k i) as [h|h].
  - destruct (compare k (1+i)) as [[hlt|heq]|hgt]; cbn.
    + reflexivity.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + exfalso. lia.
  - destruct (compare k i) as [[hlt|heq]|hgt]; cbn.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma insert_relocate_Sk : forall i k, insert_Var (Var 0) (relocate i (S k) 1) k = Var i.
Proof.
  intros. unfold insert_Var, relocate.
  destruct (test (S k) i) as [h|h].
  - destruct (compare k (1+i)) as [[hlt|heq]|hgt]; cbn.
    + reflexivity.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + exfalso. lia.
  - destruct (compare k i) as [[hlt|heq]|hgt]; cbn.
    + exfalso. lia.
    + subst. cbn. f_equal. lia.
    + reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma subst_lift_rec : forall X k u, subst_rec (lift_rec X k 1) u k = X.
Proof.
  induction X; intros k u; simpl.
  - apply insert_relocate_k.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
  - f_equal; [apply IHX1 | apply IHX2].
  - reflexivity.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
  - f_equal; [apply IHX1 | apply IHX2].
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
Qed.

Lemma subst_lift_rec_S : forall X k, subst_rec (lift_rec X (S k) 1) (Var 0) k = X.
Proof.
  induction X; intros k; simpl.
  - apply insert_relocate_Sk.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
  - f_equal; [apply IHX1 | apply IHX2].
  - reflexivity.
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
  - f_equal; [apply IHX1 | apply IHX2].
  - f_equal. apply IHX.
Qed.

Lemma subst_lift1 : forall X u, subst (lift 1 X) u = X.

Lemma subst_lift_rec11 : forall X, subst (lift_rec X 1 1) (Var 0) = X.

Lemma quant_stem_comm : forall u, subtype (Stem (Quant u)) (Quant (Stem u)).

  - change (subtype (Quant (Stem (Quant (lift_rec u 1 1)))) (Quant (Stem u))).

    + apply (sub_inst (lift_rec u 1 1) (Var 0)).
    + rewrite subst_lift_rec11. apply sub_zero.
Qed.

Lemma fork_quant_comm : forall A a, subtype (Fork A (Quant a)) (Quant (Fork (lift 1 A) a)).

    + apply sub_zero.
    + eapply sub_trans.

Qed.

  - apply fork_quant_comm.

------------------------------------------------------
subst_subtype :
  forall P Q w, subtype P Q -> subtype (subst P w) (subst Q w).
lift_subtype :
  forall P Q k n, subtype P Q -> subtype (lift_rec P k n) (lift_rec Q k n).
Prove by induction on the subtype derivation.  All rules are schematic, so
the only work is commuting subst/lift with the constructors:

      subst_rec (lift_rec X (S k) 1) (Var 0) k = X  (subst_lift_rec_S)
  - sub_inst needs the "subst commutes with subst under one binder" instance
    (two substitutions at different depths); prove the standard lemma
      subst_rec (lift_rec X 0 1) (subst ...) ...
    or avoid it by applying the induction hypothesis at the right instance.
Everything else is congruence (sub_stem/sub_fork/sub_asf/sub_funty/sub_quant
and the quantifier commutation rules are preserved verbatim by subst/lift,
because subst/lift recursively map constructors to the same constructors and
commute with Quant by incrementing the cutoff).

-------------------------------------------------------------
below_leaf : subtype T Leaf -> T = Leaf.
no_leaf_stem : subtype Leaf (Stem B) -> False.
no_leaf_fork : subtype Leaf (Fork P Q) -> False.
no_stem_fork : subtype (Stem A) (Fork P Q) -> False.
no_stem_leaf : subtype (Stem A) Leaf -> False  (from below_leaf).
stem_inv : subtype (Stem A) (Stem B) -> subtype A B.
All are proved by induction on the derivation plus inversion on the possible
last rules (which are syntactic: the constructors of the conclusion fix the
head of the source).  sub_trans is handled by applying the IH to the second
premise (whose source is the same head) and then to the first premise.

Lemma stem_quant_lift : forall a b,
  subtype (Stem a) b -> subtype (Stem (Quant a)) (Quant b).
Proof. intros a b H. eapply sub_trans.

  - apply sub_quant, H. Qed.

Proof. intros A a b H. eapply sub_trans.
